text:
Connor O'Brien: Planning to flip the provisioning pipeline feature flag to prod today. Thread for rollout steps + monitoring + rollback. Please sanity check.

Connor O'Brien: Context: this is the new provision-to-ready pipeline (state machine + readiness gates). Flag introduced in PR-48244 (staging-only initially). Fixes we wanted before prod: race condition around Ready/perf-canary (PR-48245) + routing gate consumes Ready-only (PR-48234).

Vanessa Ortiz: :eyes: Following. We can be on point for the first prod run. Agree on Ready-only semantics (no routing until Ready).

Rafael Mendes: SRE here. I’m ok moving forward *if* we treat this as staged enablement (allowlist pools) + have clear rollback. Also want to ensure alerting is in place for stuck stages.

Connor O'Brien: Proposed rollout plan (today):
1) Merge/confirm deployed: PR-48245 (Ready gating fix), PR-48241 (retry/backoff), PR-48242 (operator error messages). Confirm control-plane deploy includes these.
2) Confirm dashboards/alerts deployed: observability-pack PR-1204 (provisioning stages + time-to-ready) + stuck-stage alerts.
3) Enable feature flag in prod for **internal pool only** (redwood-dedicated-int-usw2) and run a no-op expansion (+2 nodes) via CLI.
4) If green, expand allowlist to 1 customer expansion window already scheduled (Vanessa has the pool id in her doc).
5) Leave default OFF for all other pools for 24h.

Ethan Park: Re (1) control-plane build in prod has PR-48245 + PR-48246 already. PR-48241 landed yesterday and should be in the same train. I can double check the deployed SHA.

DeployBot: prod-control-plane deploy started (train-2024-02-28.3) requested by @ethan. ETA 12m.

Ravi Menon: Routing side: guard is in prod since last week. Routing only advertises pools with state==Ready. We also added a counter for rejected states (Requested/Provisioning/Imaging/Bootstrapping/Validating).

Aisha Bello: Dashboards are up in prod. Main one: "Dedicated Provisioning — Time to Ready". Key panels to watch during rollout:
- time_to_ready_seconds (p50/p95)
- stage_duration_seconds{stage=...}
- provisioning_failures_total by stage+error_category
- provisioning_runs_stuck{stage=...} (alert)

Sergio Costa: +1. Alert thresholds in prod right now:
- WARNING: stage stuck > 45m (creates ticket)
- PAGE: stage stuck > 90m for prod pool OR failure rate > 30% over 30m
We can tune after first day.

Allison Grant: Quick reminder: watch metric cardinality for pool_id/customer_id labels. The PR includes safeguards, but if you see metric explosion in Mimir, ping me.

Gabe Wilson: For the CLI run, use:
`redwoodctl fleet provision --pool redwood-dedicated-int-usw2 --add-nodes 2 --reason "prod-flag-canary"`
It prints a run_id + dashboard link. If something goes wrong, you can re-run a single stage:
`redwoodctl fleet provision rerun --run-id <id> --stage validating`

Connor O'Brien: Rollout checklist (copy/paste):
- [ ] Confirm prod control-plane has PR-48245 included (no Ready until perf-canary completed)
- [ ] Confirm feature flag key + default: `fleet_provisioner_v2_enabled=false` globally
- [ ] Confirm allowlist for internal pool only
- [ ] Run internal pool expansion (+2 nodes)
- [ ] Verify state transitions: Requested -> ... -> Validating -> Ready
- [ ] Verify perf-canary readiness suite executed + passed (summary JSON attached in run logs)
- [ ] Verify routing did NOT advertise until Ready (routing rejected-state metric stays nonzero until Ready)
- [ ] Verify time-to-ready metrics present (overall + per-stage)
- [ ] Verify Slack bot updates in #eng-infra aren’t spamming/duplicating

Vanessa Ortiz: On the Slack bot: we saw duplicates in staging once. Is the fix in? (incident-bot PR-356 / redwood PR-48240?)

Connor O'Brien: PR-48240 is in this train; duplicate-post fix was in incident-bot PR-356 (already deployed last Friday). Worst case we can disable the bot posting without disabling provisioning.

Rafael Mendes: Rollback criteria (please make explicit):
- Any customer-impacting symptom (5xx during validation window, or routing sees non-Ready capacity) => disable flag immediately.
- >1 prod provisioning run stuck >90m OR repeated failures in the same stage with no progress after 2 retries => disable flag + fall back to legacy runbook.
- Any sign that Ready can be set without perf-canary PASS => disable flag + page Platform (this is the scary one).

Connor O'Brien: Agree. Proposed rollback steps:
1) Flip `fleet_provisioner_v2_enabled=false` (global) OR remove allowlist entry for the pool.
2) Pause any in-flight runs: `redwoodctl fleet provision pause --run-id <id>` (admin-only)
3) If needed, continue using legacy manual steps for the specific pool expansion (runbook link)
4) File Linear + note run_id + error_category for follow-up.

Priya Natarajan: +1, and please keep the blast radius small. Internal pool first, then single customer. Also ensure comms is clear: capacity isn’t usable until Ready (Validating is not routable).

DeployBot: prod-control-plane deploy finished успешно. Version: train-2024-02-28.3 (includes PR-48245, PR-48241, PR-48242).

Ethan Park: Confirmed deployed SHA includes PR-48245. Also confirming Ready transition is guarded on perf-canary completion + all readiness checks.

Connor O'Brien: Great. Next: I’m going to enable allowlist for `redwood-dedicated-int-usw2` only. @Vanessa can you run the canary expansion when ready?

Vanessa Ortiz: Yep. I’ll run in ~10m once I have Harish online to watch the infra side.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll be watching the stuck-stage dashboard + error categories. If we hit WARNING thresholds but things are progressing, we can hold. If it pages, we rollback.

Aisha Bello: Linking dashboards (prod):
- Time-to-ready overview: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-ttready
- Stage events explorer: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-provisioning-events

Sergio Costa: Also check logs for correlation IDs:
`service=fleet-provisioner env=prod run_id=<id>`
The run_id should tie through to terraform wrapper logs + perf-canary summary.

Vanessa Ortiz: Running now.
`redwoodctl fleet provision --pool redwood-dedicated-int-usw2 --add-nodes 2 --reason "prod-flag-canary"`
Got run_id: prun_01HQZ6M8F3K1YV2A6Z. Dashboard link printed.

Gabe Wilson: Watching. You should see Imaging start in ~2-3 mins after Terraform apply output.

Ravi Menon: Routing metric check: rejected_states_total increasing as expected while in Provisioning/Imaging. Once Ready flips, advertise event should fire.

Rafael Mendes: Seeing stage durations come through. Imaging looks a little slow but within normal.

Vanessa Ortiz: Update: Bootstrapping completed, now Validating. Perf-canary kicked off.

Aisha Bello: Perf-canary panel shows running (readiness_suite). Thresholds look good so far.

Connor O'Brien: If perf-canary passes + Ready flips cleanly, we proceed to customer allowlist for the scheduled window (single pool). If anything weird, we stop here.

Vanessa Ortiz: Perf-canary PASS. State flipped to Ready at 1709915979. Routing started advertising after Ready (no early traffic).

Ravi Menon: Confirmed in routing logs: advertise event at Ready, and no traffic before.

Rafael Mendes: No alerts fired. p95 time-to-ready for this run is in line with expectation.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: Next step is enabling allowlist for the customer expansion window (one pool only) later today. We’ll do that in a separate mini-checklist and keep global default OFF for 24h.

Allison Grant: Nice. Please drop the run_id + timings in the rollout doc; it’ll help when we compare before/after.

Connor O'Brien: Will do. Keeping thread open for the customer window later.
